text:
Alex DeBrincat is a shooter who doesn't stop, and that's the right instinct right now. He has 66 shots in 18 games and 7.4 expected goals, chances in line with last season's 41-goal year. The finish has lagged: 10.6% shooting against a talent range centred on 13.4%.

His last ten games brought two goals and seven points, and nothing in the last three as Detroit lost three in a row, ending with a 4-0 loss in Colorado. That's the slump. Underneath it, Detroit takes 57% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on, and our wins-added measure still ranks him 15th of 506 skaters.

Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among 401 forwards last season at 3.5 wins, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 98th percentile for chances from the slot. The Farmington Hills native is carrying a big load for his hometown team in a season dominated by Dylan Larkin's refusal to play until he's traded. Our projection says 38 goals; the shots say the goals will come.
headline: DeBrincat keeps shooting through a cold stretch
